entities.summary:
Dell is an American multinational computer technology company founded by Michael Dell in 1984 and long headquartered in Round Rock, Texas. Its direct-to-consumer PC model and build-to-order supply chain disrupted retail computer sales in the 1990s.

Through servers, storage, and later enterprise acquisitions (including EMC), Dell moved from dorm-room PCs to a full IT infrastructure vendor, navigating the post-PC era via privatisation and return to public markets. The brand became synonymous with scalable commodity computing.

Dell’s rise charts how American logistics and inventory innovation remade the personal-computer industry.
